title: Required Apps Never Started — ESP Apps Gate Starved
description: One or more required user-ESP apps never started installing while the ESP AccountSetup apps gate waited on them — the agent observed the ESP page exit with those apps still in a non-terminal, never-started state. Unlike ANALYZE-APP-015 (which reports that completion was DEFERRED because of a pending app, and stays silent once the session reaches a terminal verdict) this rule reports the delivery gap itself and fires regardless of the final outcome: an enrollment that Windows called done while required apps never ran is a successful enrollment with missing software, and the operator must see it.
author: Autopilot Monitor
explanation:
At least one **required** app assigned to the user ESP never started installing. The Intune Management Extension never moved it out of its initial state (`{{state}}`) — it did not download, did not install, and did not fail — while the ESP AccountSetup apps gate was waiting on it. First app observed: `{{appName}}`.

Every starved app has its own `app_install_starved` timeline event carrying `appId`, `appName` and `state` — open the timeline and filter on that event type for the complete list.

This is a **delivery** problem, not an install error, and it is invisible in the Intune console: the app simply never appears. Typical causes:

- far more required apps targeted at the ESP than the gate can service in the available window,
- requirement rules that are never met on this device (OS / architecture / registry / script checks),
- an unsatisfied dependency or supersedence chain,
- an app that needs a context unavailable during provisioning (e.g. a VPN client waiting on a portal sign-in),
- a mid-ESP reboot that cut the gate short — check whether the mid-ESP reboot advisory also fired for this session.

Note that this finding is independent of the session verdict. A session can be marked **Succeeded** and still be missing every app listed here.

remediation.title: Shrink the ESP blocking set
steps: Open the Enrollment Status Page profile and review the blocking app list — every required app there must finish before the user reaches the desktop.
Move apps that do not have to be present at first logon from *required* to *available*, or remove them from the ESP's blocking apps selection.
Prefer a small, deliberately chosen blocking set (security agent, VPN, management tooling) over the full application catalogue.

remediation.title: Unblock the individual apps
steps: Collect the app names from the `app_install_starved` timeline events in this session.
For each app, review its requirement rules and dependencies in Intune — IntuneManagementExtension.log records every requirement evaluation.
Verify the assignment actually targets the signed-in user (user-targeted apps need an established Entra user affinity; check the hybrid user-affinity finding if it also fired).
Re-run an enrollment and confirm the apps now reach a terminal state before the ESP exits.

remediation.title: Rule out a truncated gate
steps: Check whether a mid-ESP reboot was observed for this session — a forced restart during AccountSetup cuts the apps gate short and can starve everything still queued.
If so, reassign the reboot-forcing device policies to user groups so the restart lands after AccountSetup.
